title: Forget Dropshipping. Be The Middleman For $800+/Job (Drop-Servicing)
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Guest promotes his own company (texaslabguys.com) and asks for commercial real estate and concrete leveling contacts. The headline '$9,000 job' and '100,000 of profit in 6 months' framing is the host's hype. The business is only 90 days old, and most forward numbers are goals, not results.

stated_problem.quote: you're trying to remove tripping hazards or a liability standpoint, there's aesthetics or vanity, you want your house to look good
stated_problem.speaker: Jeff

idea.name: Drop-serviced concrete leveling
idea.one_liner: Homeowners (and some property managers) find a concrete leveling brand through Facebook ads and organic channels. The founder quotes the jobs remotely from photos, then subcontracts the foam-lift work to local trailer owners and keeps a 30-40% gross margin.
idea.customer: Residential homeowners with sunken driveways, sidewalks and walkways; secondarily HOA and property managers, with commercial and municipal jobs as a future target
idea.offer: Polyurethane foam concrete leveling at a fraction of replacement cost, with guaranteed quality and strong communication
idea.revenue_model: Per-job pricing (average about $2,500). The sub is paid about $600-700 on small jobs, the founder keeps about $1,000 average gross profit, and takes a 50% deposit upfront.

key_quotes.quote: $2,200 to fix 12 ft of a walkway even from the street to my house?
I can get you the next level without you having to do any additional work.
my hypothesis on doing everything remotely and virtually is that I can crank out five or 10 quotes
seeing those through to fulfillment is something that I'm not personally involved in a whole lot.
they have to send pictures and check-ins in order to do that.
the ease of a lead coming in and then setting up automations to reach out to that person is pretty low-hanging fruit.
So, when you're subbing it out, you make the same amount of gross profit, but you do less work.

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook ad campaign (lead form) at about $4.60 per lead, switched on and off
Google organic search to a Replit-built landing page with forms and chatbots
Outbound texting campaigns to HOA managers and property managers who oversee multiple properties
Speed to lead: an automated HighLevel AI text right after a form fill, then a phone call. Quotes are done remotely from customer photos.

ideas.delivery: Local owner-operator foam-leveling subcontractors (often veterans who own HMI trailers) do the physical work and send photo check-ins. The founder handles marketing, remote quoting, scheduling and customer communication, and is rarely on site.

tools: HighLevel (CRM + AI text bot, unlimited sub-accounts tier)
prices: $600-$700 sub cost / $1,000+ charge on small jobs

ideas.other_uk_rules: The main channels (Facebook ads, organic, inbound) are fine. Outbound texting to HOA or property managers would breach PECR if the recipient is an individual or sole trader; in the UK, reach property management firms by cold email to limited companies with an opt-out instead. Texting inbound leads after a form fill is fine with consent. UK GDPR applies to lead and photo data. Using subcontractors means checking their public liability insurance, and a 50% deposit means consumer contract and cancellation rules apply (Consumer Contracts Regulations, 14-day cancellation for off-premises or distance sales).

idea.name: Subcontracted power-wash add-on/upsell
idea.one_liner: Each residential leveling job comes with a free power wash, subcontracted to a cheap local power washer. The founder then texts the customer an upsell for extra areas (for example, a backyard for $100).
idea.offer: Free driveway and sidewalk power wash 2-3 days after leveling, with paid add-ons for other areas
idea.revenue_model: Cost ($100-150) is built into the leveling quote; small paid upsells cover it

key_quotes.quote: another thing I do for residential jobs is I throw in a free power wash on the area.
So, it's a small upsell to potentially cover the cost.

acquisition_channels.details: Upsell by text to existing leveling customers after a good experience

ideas.delivery: A subcontracted local power-washing provider does the work 2-3 days after the leveling job
ideas.other_uk_rules: Upsell texts to existing customers rely on the PECR soft opt-in, so offer an opt-out in every message.

idea.name: Concrete-leveling-as-a-service contracts
idea.one_liner: An annual, insurance-like contract for property managers, home builders and multi-site retail landlords that covers a set amount of concrete leveling per property, priced in six figures.
idea.customer: Commercial and industrial property managers, new home builders, owners of multiple retail properties
idea.offer: An annual allowance of concrete leveling per property (for example, one free job per property per month), pitched as preventing trip-and-fall liability
idea.revenue_model: High-ticket annual contract budgeted in advance (six figures)

key_quotes.quote: I want to be an insurance-like product that gives them up to a certain amount of concrete leveling at each of their properties on an annualized basis.
that way I can create more predictability to my top line, and I also will have higher utilization and justification to own more assets.

claims.claim: Planned contracts priced in six figures per year
claims.quote: I want to sell it as a higher-ticket item that's in the six figures

acquisition_channels.details: Planned: relationships with property managers and real estate firms, with a liability/fear-based pitch (not yet executed)

ideas.delivery: Subcontracted or owned leveling crews serve the contracted properties
ideas.other_uk_rules: B2B outreach should use cold email to limited companies (with opt-out) or TPS/CTPS-screened calls. Recurring B2B contracts fall outside the DMCC consumer subscription rules.
